newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Northeast power softer on Maine nuke startup.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Northeast power softer on Maine nuke startup.

text.p: Spot wholesale electricity prices in the northeastern U.S. ended softer Friday ahead of the U.S. Columbus Day weekend and amid news of the startup of the Maine Yankee nuclear power plant, market sources said.
On expectations of more generating capacity returning to the New England Power Pool (NEPOOL), sellers were pressured to lower their spot values, traders said.
"Sellers were hoping to put off sales," said a Northeast power trader,
Maine Yankee Atomic Power Co said the 910 MW nuclear generating station in Wiscasset, Maine, could restart as early as this weekend after tripping off line during testing on Wednesday.
Daily power trading for the weekend and Monday was thin with a number of players sold out for the week, they said.

Ongoing testing this weekend at the 584 megawatt (MW) Canal Generating Station unit 2 in Sandwich, Mass., produced excess energy and downward pressure on spot NEPOOL power prices, market sources said.

Peak, non-firm electricity for weekend delivery in NEPOOL at the Northeast Utilities territory border was assessed at $28.00-$30.00 a megawatt hour (MWh), and for Monday delivery $31.00-$32.00, lower than Thursday's quote of $33.00.
Off-peak, non-firm NEPOOL power for the weekend at the NU border was valued at $19.00-$20.00 and for Monday $21.00-$22.00, compared with $22.00 on Thursday.

In the New York Power Pool (NYPP), peak, non-firm power delivered in the western part of the system for the weekend was quoted at $17.00-$18.00 a MWh and for Monday $19.00-$20.00, compared with Thursday's quote near $19.00.
Off-peak, non-firm, western NYPP electricity for the weekend was discussed near $13.00 a MWh and for Monday near $14.00, down from a range of $13.00-$14.00 on Thursday.
In eastern NYPP, peak, non-firm electricity was talked near $23.00 a MWh for this weekend and $26.00-$27.00 for Monday, compared with Thursday's $24.00-$27.00 delivery for Friday.
Off-peak, non-firm power in eastern NYPP for the weekend was quoted near $15.00 and for Monday $15.50-$16.60, down from Thursday's $18.50-$19.00 range.
The latest forecasts showed temperatures in most of the Northeast would peak in the high 50's Fahrenheit degree range and bottom in the low 30's.
